item.name: A Feast for Odin
item.comment: The first big expansion (the Norwegians) will be published at the fairy in Essen 2018. New animals (pigs breed every round, horses count 6 VP), new islands, new bothsides unique barns (random-start-piece for every player), new flipable, three-piece-action board (with a "last action"-row and new action-possiblities like elk-hunting, little emigration and theft by a knorr) for 1-2, 3 and 4 players, more almanac-infos about the viking-time and some more... Deeper and new strategies to discover!

item.name: A Feast for Odin: Lofoten, Orkney, and Tierra del Fuego
item.comment: The fishing area of Lofoten got in viking focus since 600 AD. The Orkney-archipelago since 780 AD. The "Tierra del Fuego" - in german "Feuerland" is a reminiscence to the publishing firm "Feuerland" and has no historical counterpart. Its backside is "Feuerland" by night, because it was called so from Magellan by seeing many fires of eboriginies in the next 20 nights on the island-side. Detailed infos will come with a little almanac in the First Expansion - The Norwegians that will be published at the fair Essen 2018. It includes also the four basic-game islands with the new grafic elements from the mini-expansion. It will bring too, four new islands (Outer Hebrides, Isle of Skye, Isle of man, Islay) and on the backside coastal viking-founded "cities"/longphorts in Ireland (Wexford, Waterford) and viking trading points ( Cork, Limerick). These can be used with the basic game, but are also developed for the great new possiblitites of the expansion like the new action-board (with a new, fifth dolumn of a "last action" and totally new ideas like theft by the trading ship "knorr"), new sheds (everybody gets a unique two-sided random min-borad that can be build for one action), new puzzle-pieces/animals (pig+horse) and other elements (little emigration piece,...) that give new experiences and totally new strategie-elements. Therefor some action-boards elements of the basic games are also changed a bit and some old islands have diffent victory-points. Again well balanced and tested (I hope so). There are no new handcards, but handcards now can be "thown away" vor victory-points (2-4 VP). I started the testing of expansion elements already before the basic game was published.

item.name: Fields of Arle: New Travel Destination – Aachen
item.comment:
Aachen is an old city of much historical impact (residence of Charles le magne) nowadays at the three-country corner Germany/Netherlands/Belgium about 50+ km West of Cologne.
The tile has three great offers, 3 food for clay is unique and comparable to standard tile offer peat (Torf/ Plattdeutsch Turf) -> 3 food (Emden). 6 food for a by peat uptraded clay/ a brick is also great (also offered in Adendorf). 4 food for leather/wool fabrics is standard (Aurich/Esens), but the option to get 4 food is only possible at Bremen (with leather+wool fabrics to 12 food). In Leer you get only 3 food for it.
PS: I work on a Jeverland expansion with new kinds of trading options like linen (1vp)+flax to summer cloths (2vp) in Varel (historical place for hugher cloth making).

item.name: Robinson Crusoe: Adventures on the Cursed Island – Mystery Tales
item.comment: Great game again. But you will need lot of time for getting answers to so many questions, that haven't been explained in the rules. The publisher/author made here again no good job and BGG is needed here for sure to study. A learning curve to critics for the basic game does not exist. A lost chance also to answer the FAQs in that expansion. The rules do get a 4-5, the game a 10. Also the description is sometimes bad. For example no explaining on which dice to stick on the new stickers (stick it on hurting dice) and the "green" sticker with transparence get black on the red dice. A simple appendix (like for example in Feast for Odin) with explaining all possible problems of any card in details would have been so helpful. I also missed the victory point system from basic game hardly at the end of Z campaign. You just win or loose. Why downgrading a game at this important point? Great option: You can play older scenarios again with new elements/roles/horror modus.

item.comment: The computer game is really great and would be rated a 10. The board game is close to the pc-story, maybe to close for people knowing the pc-game. Its focus is on the home, while the night tours are more abstract and made by a textbook in DSA-solo style .> looking for nearly 2000 numbers. Made for to start playing without long rule studying it has the problem that you need to remember all or search in the 2000 numbers for a forgotten rule that is not explained enough in the day-scale mini.rulebook. An additional backup rulebook would have been helpful or minimum a page of most important things as an overview. We missed for example the door opening dice number of sucess (1-5 is fail).

item.name: Viticulture
item.comment: You need the expansion too, that I do rate a 9.2. Same to moorfarmer card expansion from Uwe Rosenberg => 9.4 rating than. The basic game itself isn't such exciting and some people might not buy the expansion therefore later, but its worth any penny. Buy both together, no mistake. In the German version from Feuerland you have directly this + some elements of Tuscany. That's much better! Windmill and tasting room are much to expensive: Recommanded houserule: Reduce costs by 2. Otherwise nobody would build them in general (only maybe with a card trick, but not because of its function). Sadly the author didn't agree in changing this at my point of view really big mistake for the German version Feuerland did make. However, this big mistake of being unbalanced doesn't really hurt the game, if you simply do not build them. If the income element for the wine would have been renewed too to a relevant element (you just get some money, when its irrelevant close to game end), I would rate it a 9.5. I still hope for a rebalanced version in the future.

item.name: Wingspan
item.comment: Deeper gameplay in a quicker form than on other worker placements. Good choice in lack of time to play "bigger" workerplacements ;-) In Germany in the race for "Kennerspiel des Jahres" price. For good luck most people didn't realize a hugh bug. Most people in chessclub didn't want to play it again after realizing that bug: Some cards (egg based, no/low costs) are overpowered and you win easier with one (~+25%) and in about 80-90% with two of them. I made a new set of start cards to reduce this problem to an acceptable size. This mini-expansion didn't find yet its way to the audience...
